target.title: fix(acp): defer session snapshot update after newSession/resumeSession result
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where ACP clients could receive `session_info_update` and `available_commands_update` notifications before the `session/new` or `session/resume` JSON-RPC response, causing the client to observe incomplete session state on the wire. The deferred notifications could also fire after `session/close` completed, sending stale session_info_update notifications for sessions the client had already closed.

## Why This Change Was Made

`setTimeout(0)` defers initial lifecycle notifications past the synchronous handler return and response serialization, establishing a deterministic event-loop boundary that guarantees the JSON-RPC result reaches the wire before any notification. A `hasSession` guard at the top of each deferred callback skips stale notifications when `closeSession` has already removed the session from the store, closing the close-before-timer race window. Boundary: `src/acp/translator.ts` lifecycle handlers only — Gateway protocol layer, session storage, prompt handling, and other ACP handlers are unchanged.

## User Impact

ACP clients can now rely on receiving the `session/new` and `session/resume` JSON-RPC result before any `session/update` notification over the wire, and will no longer receive stale notifications for sessions they have already closed. No user-visible API or response shape changes.

## Evidence

### Cross-Process NDJSON Wire Transcript — newSession

A real ACP server child process (separate Node process) imports `AcpGatewayAgent` + `AgentSideConnection` + `ndJsonStream` over real stdio pipes. The parent process acts as the ACP client, sending JSON-RPC via stdin and capturing raw NDJSON bytes from the child's stdout. This is real cross-process proof, not in-process simulation.

```
[0] {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{"protocolVersion":1,"agentCapabilities":{...},"agentInfo":{"name":"openclaw-acp","title":"OpenClaw ACP Gateway","version":"2026.7.2"},"authMethods":[]}}
    ↑ initialize RESPONSE

[1] {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"result":{"sessionId":"a943ce9f-63de-4876-85f5-8a86129a1145","configOptions":[...],"modes":{...}}}
    ↑ session/new RESULT ← arrives FIRST (real wire bytes from child stdout)

[2] {"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"session/update","params":{"sessionId":"a943ce9f-...","update":{"sessionUpdate":"session_info_update","title":"acp-bridge:...","updatedAt":null,"_meta":{"sessionKey":"acp-bridge:...","kind":"unknown"}}}}
    ↑ session_info_update NOTIFICATION ← arrives AFTER response
```

**Ordering proof**: response index [1] < notification index [2]. ✓

### Cross-Process NDJSON Wire Transcript — resumeSession

```
[0] {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{"protocolVersion":1,"agentCapabilities":{...},"agentInfo":{"name":"openclaw-acp","title":"OpenClaw ACP Gateway","version":"2026.7.2"},"authMethods":[]}}
    ↑ initialize RESPONSE

[1] {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"result":{"configOptions":[...],"modes":{"currentModeId":"adaptive","availableModes":[...]}}}
    ↑ session/resume RESULT ← arrives FIRST (real wire bytes from child stdout)

[2] {"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"session/update","params":{"sessionId":"agent:main:process-proof","update":{"sessionUpdate":"session_info_update","title":"Process proof session","updatedAt":"2026-07-19T03:45:03.302Z","_meta":{"sessionKey":"agent:main:process-proof","kind":"direct","spawnedWorkspaceDir":"/tmp"}}}}
    ↑ session_info_update NOTIFICATION ← arrives AFTER response
```

**Ordering proof**: response index [1] < notification index [2]. ✓

### Cross-Process Test Run

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/acp/translator.lifecycle.process-proof.test.ts

 ✓ |acp| src/acp/translator.lifecycle.process-proof.test.ts (2 tests) 6795ms
     ✓ newSession: response line precedes session/update notification across process boundary
     ✓ resumeSession: response line precedes session/update notification across process boundary

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed (2)
```

### Close-Before-Timer Regression Tests

Two tests verify the close race guard:

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/acp/translator.lifecycle.test.ts

 ✓ |acp| src/acp/translator.lifecycle.test.ts (17 tests) 265ms
     ✓ newSession suppresses deferred notifications when closeSession runs before the timer fires
     ✓ resumeSession suppresses deferred notifications when closeSession runs before the timer fires
```

Both tests call `newSession`/`resumeSession`, immediately call `closeSession` before the deferred timer fires, flush the timer queue, and assert `sessionUpdate` is never called.

### Full Test Run

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/acp/translator.lifecycle.test.ts src/acp/translator.lifecycle.ndjson-proof.test.ts src/acp/translator.lifecycle.process-proof.test.ts

 ✓ |acp| src/acp/translator.lifecycle.test.ts (17 tests) 265ms
 ✓ |acp| src/acp/translator.lifecycle.ndjson-proof.test.ts (2 tests) 11687ms
 ✓ |acp| src/acp/translator.lifecycle.process-proof.test.ts (2 tests) 6795ms

 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  21 passed (21)
```

### Lint Fix

3x `eslint(no-promise-executor-return)` violations in `translator.lifecycle.test.ts` fixed by wrapping `setTimeout` in a block body:

```diff
- await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 0));
+ await new Promise((resolve) => { setTimeout(resolve, 0); });
```

### Type Safety Fix

2x `TS2345` errors in `translator.lifecycle.ndjson-proof.test.ts` under `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` fixed by extracting `const line = arr[i]` with `if (!line) continue` guard.

### Environment

- OS: Linux
- Node: 24.15.0
- Branch: `fix/acp-bridge-session-order`
- OpenClaw: `2026.7.2`
- Server entry: `src/acp/acp-server-process-for-proof.ts` (real child process)
- Client: vitest parent process spawning the server via `child_process.spawn`

### What Was Not Tested

Real OpenClaw Gateway WebSocket connection (requires Gateway credentials/infra). The cross-process proof uses a mock Gateway client inside the server child process, but the ACP transport is fully real: separate Node process, real stdio pipes, real `ndJsonStream` byte serialization, real process boundary. The ordering guarantee being proven is purely an ACP transport-level property, independent of Gateway backing.
